clause_inventory.source_paraphrase: On 24 March 2025, a WhatsApp sender impersonating the company’s chief financial officer arranged a restructuring discussion. A purported lawyer stressed confidentiality and obtained a non-disclosure agreement.

On 25 March, the finance director joined a rescheduled Zoom call with deepfake executive impersonators. That call and later messages from the purported lawyer supplied instructions for the payment made the following day.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The synthetic executives supplied the materially false corporate authority context on which the victim relied when transferring funds, while police evidence later supported recovery.
Deepfake executives in a Zoom meeting supplied false senior authority to the finance director, who transferred more than US$499,000.

The reported deepfake executive call materially implemented the false corporate instruction and was followed by the finance director’s payment. The matched call, instructions and payment establish impaired informed choice; a human-selected tactic is eligible under the current criteria.

clause_inventory.source_paraphrase: On 26 March, the director transferred more than US$499,000 to a local corporate mule account. More than US$494,000 then went to Hong Kong accounts.
A further request for US$1.4 million on 27 March prompted discovery. The director alerted HSBC, which notified Singapore’s Anti-Scam Centre.
On 28 March, Hong Kong police withheld the amount transferred there, and Singapore police seized more than US$5,000 remaining locally. The police release described an ongoing investigation.
